bueno:A.tip: un buen libro = a good book
bueno:A.more: Bueno usually shortens to buen before a masculine singular noun, even with an intervening adjective. It stays bueno in el bueno de Pedro; shortening is optional when coordinated with another adjective. Buena does not shorten. Mejor is the usual comparative and has a separate card.

malo:A.tip: Mal can also be the adverb badly.
malo:A.more: Malo shortens to mal before a masculine singular noun. Mala does not shorten. Mal the adverb is a separate use.

grande:A.tip: Same singular form for both genders.
grande:A.more: Grande usually shortens to gran before a singular noun of either gender. It stays grande after más or menos; some coordinated or muy constructions allow either form.

actual:A.tip: Current, not the usual English meaning of actual.

actualmente:R.tip: Currently; not actually in the sense of in fact.

realizar:V.tip: Usually carry out; not realize in the sense of become aware.

pretender:V.tip: Usually intend or aim; not pretend in the sense of act falsely.

asistir:V.tip: To attend; not usually assist in the sense of help.

conocer:V.tip: Familiarity; compare saber for knowledge of facts.

saber:V.tip: Knowledge or knowing how; compare conocer.

buscar:V.tip: No por is needed to translate look for.

pedir:V.tip: To ask for something; preguntar is to ask a question.

escuchar:V.tip: Listen to something; with a specific person, use personal a: escuchar a Ana.

depender:V.tip: Spanish uses de where English uses on.

consistir:V.tip: Spanish uses en where English often uses of.

insistir:V.tip: Learn the preposition with the verb.

acordar:V.tip: Agree on something; acordarse de means remember.

recordar:V.tip: No de in this pattern; compare acordarse de.

acabar:V.tip: With a present form: to have just done something.

tratar:V.tip: To try to do something; tratar de + a topic means be about that topic.

referir:V.tip: Report something; referirse a means refer to.

gustar:V.pattern: me gusta + singular · me gustan + plural
gustar:V.tip: The thing liked is the grammatical subject.

interesar:V.tip: The thing that interests you is the grammatical subject.

importar:V.tip: For matter: the thing that matters is the subject.

costar:V.tip: The thing that costs is the grammatical subject.

faltar:V.tip: The thing missing is the grammatical subject.

sentar:V.tip: Seat someone; sentarse means sit down.

casar:V.tip: Casarse means get married; con introduces the partner.

despedir:V.tip: Dismiss/fire; despedirse de means say goodbye to.

llevar:V.tip: Often take/carry away; traer brings toward the relevant place.

traer:V.tip: Bring toward the relevant place; compare llevar.

coger:V.tip: Regional meaning matters: see the meaning above.

alguno:Q.tip: Alguno shortens to algún before a masculine singular noun.
alguno:Q.more: Algún goes before a masculine singular noun, even with an intervening adjective. It is also usual immediately before a feminine noun beginning with stressed a; that noun remains feminine.

ninguno:Q.tip: Ninguno shortens to ningún before a masculine singular noun.
ninguno:Q.more: Usually singular. Plural ningunos/ningunas is restricted to plural-only nouns, emphatic negatives and expressions such as ningunas ganas. Ningún is also usual immediately before a feminine noun beginning with stressed a.

cualquiera:Q.tip: Cualquiera shortens to cualquier before a singular noun of either gender.
cualquiera:Q.more: Cualquier goes before a singular noun of either gender. Cualesquiera is the formal plural; the shortened plural cualesquier is rare. Cualquieras belongs to a different noun use, not this quantifier.

cada:Q.tip: Each/every; cada itself does not change.

ambos:Q.tip: Both; the form agrees with the noun.
ambos:Q.more: Plural in the meaning taught here; the ending agrees with the noun.

varios:Q.tip: Several; the form agrees with the noun.
varios:Q.more: Plural in the meaning taught here; the ending agrees with the noun.

nuestro:X.tip: Agree with what is owned, not with the owners.
nuestro:X.more: Forms agree with the thing owned, not the owner. These same forms can go before or after a noun, or stand on their own.

tuyo:X.pattern: tu libro · el libro es tuyo
tuyo:X.tip: Tu has no accent; tú is the subject pronoun.
tuyo:X.more: Forms agree with the thing owned, not the owner. The short forms go before a noun; the long forms follow a noun or stand on their own.

primero:M.tip: Primero shortens to primer before a masculine singular noun.

tercero:M.tip: Tercero shortens to tercer before a masculine singular noun.

segundo:M.tip: Second in order; segundo as a time unit is a separate card.

cuarto:M.tip: Fourth in order; cuarto meaning room or quarter is a separate card.

medio:M.tip: Half; medio agrees with the noun.
medio:M.more: In this half-quantity use, medio agrees with the noun: media hora, medios litros. Adverbial medio (somewhat) does not agree; medio the noun has a separate card.

aquel:D.tip: That/those, more distant; neuter aquello stands alone.
aquel:D.more: Aquello is the neuter form: it stands alone for an idea or unidentified thing, never before a noun, and has no plural.

cuyo:H.tip: Whose: agree with the thing possessed, not its owner.

cual:H.pattern: el cual · la cual · los cuales · las cuales
cual:H.tip: Relative which/who; agree with the antecedent.
cual:H.more: The article and relative agree with the antecedent. Lo cual refers to a preceding fact or statement. Relative cual/cuales has no accent; question cuál/cuáles has its own card.

quien:H.tip: Relative who; no accent in this use.

cuánto:W.tip: How much/many; agree when accompanying a noun.
cuánto:W.more: With a noun, agree in gender and number; adverbial cuánto does not vary. Keep the accent in questions and exclamations.

cuál:W.tip: Which/which one; usage before a noun varies by region.

mientras:C.tip: While; mientras que can also contrast two statements.

sino:C.tip: Not X, but Y; si no (two words) means if not.

porque:C.tip: Because. Por qué (two words, accented) means why.

aún:R.tip: Still/yet: keep the accent. Compare aun meaning even.

aun:R.tip: Even: no accent. Compare aún meaning still/yet.

mí:L.tip: Me after a preposition; mi without an accent means my.
mí:L.more: Use conmigo for with me, not con mí. Conmigo also retains its own course card. Subject yo and object me are separate cards.

ti:L.tip: Ti has no accent. With con, use contigo.
ti:L.more: Ti has no accent. Use contigo for with you, not con ti. Subject tú and object te are separate cards.

sí:L.tip: Refers back to a third-person referent in the same sentence; with con, use consigo.
sí:L.more: Sí is unchanged for gender and number in this third-person reflexive/reciprocal use. Consigo is reflexive: with himself/herself/themselves. It is not the affirmative sí meaning yes.

usted:L.tip: Formal you uses third-person verb forms.
usted:L.more: Usted uses third-person singular verbs; ustedes uses third-person plural verbs. Ustedes is the ordinary plural you in most of Latin America, and formal plural you in most of Spain.

nosotros:L.tip: Subject we or us after a preposition; compare object nos.

os:L.tip: Object/reflexive form used with vosotros in Spain.

conmigo:L.tip: Means with me; do not add another con.

don:N.tip: Title of respect; no article in this address pattern.
don:N.more: Don and doña are titles before first names, without an article. Los dones belongs to the separate gift or talent meaning.

mil:N.tip: A thousand; miles de = thousands of.

gana:N.tip: Usually plural ganas: to feel like doing something.

gente:N.tip: Feminine singular in grammar, despite meaning people.

persona:N.tip: Always feminine in this sense, including for a man.

víctima:N.tip: Feminine, regardless of the person’s gender.

este:D.more: Esto is the neuter form: it stands alone for an idea or unidentified thing, never before a noun, and has no plural.

ese:D.more: Eso is the neuter form: it stands alone for an idea or unidentified thing, never before a noun, and has no plural.

tal:D.tip: Same form for both genders; tales is plural.

mío:X.more: Forms agree with the thing owned, not the owner. The short forms go before a noun; the long forms follow a noun or stand on their own.

suyo:X.more: Forms agree with the thing owned, not the owner. The short forms go before a noun; the long forms follow a noun or stand on their own.

mismo:Q.more: These forms agree with the noun or referent in this use.

mucho:Q.more: These forms agree with the noun or referent in this use.

poco:Q.more: These forms agree with the noun or referent in this use.

tanto:Q.more: These forms agree with the noun or referent in this use.

cierto:Q.more: These forms agree with the noun or referent in this use.

uno:Q.more: Uno/una can stand for one person or thing; unos/unas can mean some. Generic-person uno/una stays singular. In ordinary partitives, use uno de ellos but algunos de ellos for the plural. Un before a noun belongs to the article card; numeral one has its own card.

lo:L.more: Direct-object forms agree with the referent. Neuter lo can stand for an idea or statement and has no plural. The article in lo importante is a different use.

le:L.more: Le/les marks the recipient without distinguishing gender. Before lo, la, los or las, either becomes se: se lo doy. Se has its own card.

él:L.more: These are stressed third-person pronouns, used as subjects or after prepositions. Ello refers to an idea or fact and has no plural; its use is restricted. Object lo and le have their own cards.

presidente:N.more: Use the feminine forms for a female referent. Presidenta is the usual recommended feminine.
presidente:N.tip: Gender forms depend on the referent.

actor:N.more: Use the feminine forms for a female referent. Actriz is the feminine for a performer. Actora belongs to other uses, including a party in a legal case.
actor:N.tip: Gender forms depend on the referent.

miembro:N.more: For a female group member, both el miembro and la miembro are valid. El miembro can refer to a person of any gender; la miembro makes a female referent explicit.
miembro:N.tip: El miembro can refer to any gender; la miembro specifies a woman.

jefe:N.more: Use the feminine forms for a female referent. Jefa is more frequent; la jefe is also valid.
jefe:N.tip: Gender forms depend on the referent.

líder:N.more: Use the feminine forms for a female referent. La líder is widely used; lideresa is more common in parts of the Americas.
líder:N.tip: Gender forms depend on the referent.

secretario:N.more: Use the feminine forms for a female referent. Secretaria names a female secretary; secretaría with an accent is an office or department, a different noun.
secretario:N.tip: Gender forms depend on the referent.

rey:N.more: Use the feminine forms for a female referent. Reina is the feminine counterpart of rey.
rey:N.tip: Gender forms depend on the referent.

cliente:N.more: Use the feminine forms for a female referent. Both la cliente and la clienta are valid.
cliente:N.tip: Gender forms depend on the referent.

juez:N.more: Use the feminine forms for a female referent. Both la juez and la jueza are valid.
juez:N.tip: Gender forms depend on the referent.

poeta:N.more: Use the feminine forms for a female referent. Both la poeta and la poetisa are used.
poeta:N.tip: Gender forms depend on the referent.

alcalde:N.more: Use the feminine forms for a female referent. Alcaldesa is the feminine counterpart of alcalde.
alcalde:N.tip: Gender forms depend on the referent.

dirigente:N.more: Use el dirigente for a man and la dirigente for a woman; the noun itself stays the same. The plurals are los dirigentes and las dirigentes.
dirigente:N.tip: Gender forms depend on the referent.

club:N.more: Both clubes and clubs are valid plurals.

fútbol:N.more: This card teaches the sport, normally used without a plural. Plural uses for varieties of football are outside this sense.

pasado:N.more: This card teaches the past as a general time or idea, normally singular. Other countable uses are not included here.

izquierda:N.more: This card teaches the left side or direction, normally singular in expressions such as a mi izquierda. The plural appears in other uses and fixed expressions, such as a izquierdas (counterclockwise).
